plan.title: Colon treated vs control DE (RSEM counts) + enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 colon samples (6 treated, 6 control, unpaired, single batch), quantified by RSEM into gene-level expected counts (12000 genes x 12 samples; a 13th column is the gene symbol). RSEM expected counts are non-integer and length-dependent; the per-sample genes.results files carrying effective lengths were not delivered, so the tximport length-offset path (the sourced default for RSEM) cannot be run. The plan therefore rounds the expected counts to nearest integer and proceeds on the standard DESeq2 raw-count path, explicitly flagging that gene-length normalization was not applied (a caveat for genes whose length differs systematically between conditions). Sample sample_01 has ~4x lower library size than the median; per the knowledge-service rule this is kept through QC, inspected on PCA/sample-distance plots, and only dropped with a stated, evidence-based reason -- it is not removed by default. Pipeline: QC on sample structure -> minimal low-count pre-filter -> DESeq2 Wald test with explicit reference level (control) and apeglm LFC shrinkage -> BH-adjusted results with independent filtering (alpha=0.05) -> two enrichment passes (ORA with clusterProfiler enrichGO against the tested-gene universe on the significant list per the knowledge-service's binding rule for a discrete gene-list enrichment_input, plus a preranked fgsea complement on the full Wald-statistic-ranked list against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome, both staged locally) -> consolidated report with fit diagnostics, p-value histogram, reproducibility record, and explicit statement of the RSEM/length-offset limitation.
